io4_next_preflight: Before any write, make a fresh full NORMAL_NKRO baseline with same serial, rev=saved, dirty=false, valid_slots3, maintenance idle, physical_mask0, active profile4, and preserve schema2/profile bytes plus CRC.

Physically verify the BT10/GP9 recovery control and exact hold/reset/power sequence from board labeling and firmware documentation before entering IO4; ensure user can perform it immediately if CDC disappears.
Change only saved startup mode to IO4, confirm save status/revision and read back requested/saved mode before issuing one cold reboot; do not loop or retry.
Expect CDC loss in IO4. Capture USB/PnP re-enumeration and at most the authorized single HID status/report attempt; do not interpret prior HidD error1 as proof of firmware failure or success.
Use the verified physical recovery control to return to NORMAL_NKRO; confirm unique serial and CDC hello, then save NORMAL_NKRO and perform at most one target application reboot.

Finally compare complete profiles and schema snapshot against baseline, accounting for expected revision and startup mode bytes only during intermediate state; require final saved/current mode NORMAL_NKRO, active profile4, dirty false, slots3, idle, mask0, and close handles.
On any failure to recover or identity mismatch, stop; preserve evidence and do not issue repeated mode changes or flash firmware.
limitations: Observed PnP absence duration includes OS polling cadence; the user confirmation establishes unplugged-at-least-five-seconds.
This does not test power loss during Flash commit.
No IO4 operation has occurred in this review.
A single IO4 switch and recovery cannot support claims of repeated reliability, actual game compatibility, key mappings, or real HID report-byte validity.
